To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the acid hydrolysis of Maida flour is a viable method of producing reducing sugar, but that the optimal conditions for maximum yield are a 15 mL/100 ml concentration of 2 M acid and a 60-minute reaction time at 75°C.
the degradation of maida flour has significant effect on the sugar yield and the sugar yield is found to be 40-50%.
the acid hydrolysis is the best way to obtain reducing sugars from maida flour.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the bioconversion of maida (polysachharides) to reducing sugar and its estimation using three standard methods.
the bio-mimic conversion and estimation of reducing sugar in maida flour by acid hydrolyses.
the hydrolysis of polysaccharides to monosaccharides and their estimation by using Bertrand’s, Fehling, Benedict’s method.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, the hydrolysis of Maida flour (lignocellulosic biomass) to reducing sugars is a promising process and the sugar yield is 40-50%.
, maida is a good lignocellulosics material for the conversion of reducing sugars and can be used for the fermentation processes to produce value added products.
, the hydrolysis of Maida is carried out in a hotplate with the temperature of 75°C and the time of 60 min and the acid of 15 mL/100mL distilled water.

maida is a potential source of reducing sugars which can be used in various industries.
the maida flour has a potential to be used as a raw material for the conversion of polysaccharides to reducing sugars.
the hydrolysis of lignocellulosics to reducing sugars is a promising approach to produce bioethanol, biofuel, bio-chemicals, and bio-materials.

the hydrolysis of polysaccharides present in maida can be carried out using 2M sulphuric acid and hydrochloric acid.
